es.summary: Clase de fármacos hipoglucemiantes que estimulan la liberación de insulina de las células β pancreáticas.
key_points: Requieren β‑células funcionales para ser efectivas.
Principal efecto adverso: hipoglucemia, especialmente con ejercicio o alcohol.
Interaccionan con betabloqueantes que pueden enmascarar síntomas de hipoglucemia.
Se usan en diabetes tipo 2 cuando la dieta y el ejercicio no son suficientes.

mechanism: Se unen a los canales de potasio ATP‑dependientes (K⁺) en la membrana de la célula β.
Bloquean el flujo de K⁺, despolarizando la célula y abriendo canales de Ca²⁺.
El aumento de Ca²⁺ intracelular estimula la exocitosis de insulina.
indications: Diabetes mellitus tipo 2 con β‑células funcionales.
Pacientes que no alcanzan control glucémico con dieta y ejercicio solos.
contraindications: Embarazo y lactancia (excepto bajo estricto control médico).
adverse_effects: Hipoglucemia (más frecuente en ayuno, ejercicio intenso o consumo de alcohol).
interactions: Betabloqueantes: pueden ocultar temblor y taquicardia de hipoglucemia.
Otros hipoglucemiantes (insulina, GLP‑1 agonistas): potencian la hipoglucemia.
Alcohol: potencia la caída de glucosa.
Antifúngicos azólicos (ketoconazol) pueden aumentar niveles plasmáticos.
nursing_care: Evaluar glucemia capilar antes de administrar; retener si <70 mg/dL.
Monitorear glucemia cada 1‑2 h después de la dosis inicial.
Observar signos de hipoglucemia: sudoración, temblor, confusión.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si glucemia <54 mg/dL o síntomas graves.
Registrar hora de la última comida y actividad física reciente.
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento justo antes de una comida principal.
Reconocer y tratar rápidamente la hipoglucemia (ej. jugo de fruta).
Evitar consumo excesivo de alcohol y ejercicio vigoroso sin ajuste de dosis.
Informar al médico sobre uso de betabloqueantes u otros hipoglucemiantes.
No omitir comidas; si se salta una comida, consultar al profesional.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de nivel de glucemia inestable
outcomes: Control de glucemia: glucosa capilar entre 80‑130 mg/dL en 2 semanas.
Conocimiento del paciente: identifica signos de hipoglucemia y medidas correctivas.

interventions.action: Medir glucemia capilar antes de cada dosis y registrar resultados.
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar hipoglucemia precoz y ajustar la terapia.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente el uso de glucosa de acción rápida (tabletas o jugo).
interventions.rationale: Facilita la autocorrección de episodios hipoglucémicos.

interventions.action: Revisar el plan de comidas y actividad física del paciente.
interventions.rationale: Previene fluctuaciones bruscas de glucosa relacionadas con alimentos o ejercicio.

interventions.action: Evaluar la presencia de betabloqueantes y coordinar con el médico ajustes de dosis.
interventions.rationale: Los betabloqueantes pueden enmascarar síntomas de hipoglucemia.

interventions.action: Informar al paciente que informe cualquier episodio de sudoración, temblor o confusión.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección temprana y la intervención oportuna.

en.summary: Class of hypoglycemic drugs that stimulate insulin release from pancreatic β cells.
key_points: Require functional β cells to be effective.
Primary adverse effect: hypoglycemia, especially with exercise or alcohol.
Interact with beta‑blockers that can mask hypoglycemia symptoms.
Used in type 2 diabetes when diet and exercise alone are insufficient.

mechanism: Bind to ATP‑dependent potassium (K⁺) channels on the β‑cell membrane.
Block K⁺ flow, depolarizing the cell and opening Ca²⁺ channels.
The rise in intracellular Ca²⁺ stimulates insulin exocytosis.
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with functional β cells.
Patients who do not achieve glycemic control with diet and exercise alone.
contraindications: Pregnancy and lactation (except under strict medical supervision).
adverse_effects: Hypoglycemia (most common during fasting, intense exercise, or alcohol consumption).
Severe cutaneous reactions (rash, Stevens‑Johnson syndrome) – serious.
interactions: Beta‑blockers: may mask tremor and tachycardia of hypoglycemia.
Other hypoglycemics (insulin, GLP‑1 agonists): potentiate hypoglycemia.
Azole antifungals (ketoconazole) can increase plasma levels.
nursing_care: Check capillary glucose before administration; hold if <70 mg/dL.
Monitor glucose every 1‑2 h after the initial dose.
Observe for hypoglycemia signs: sweating, tremor, confusion.
Hold the dose and notify the physician if glucose <54 mg/dL or severe symptoms.
Document time of last meal and recent physical activity.
patient_teaching: Take the medication just before a main meal.
Recognize and treat hypoglycemia promptly (e.g., fruit juice).
Avoid excessive alcohol and vigorous exercise without dose adjustment.
Inform the physician about beta‑blocker or other hypoglycemic use.
Do not skip meals; if a meal is missed, consult the professional.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for unstable blood glucose level
outcomes: Blood glucose control: capillary glucose 80‑130 mg/dL within 2 weeks.
Patient knowledge: identifies hypoglycemia signs and corrective measures.

interventions.action: Measure capillary glucose before each dose and record results.
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of hypoglycemia and therapy adjustment.

interventions.action: Teach the patient how to use rapid‑acting glucose (pills or juice).
Review the patient’s meal plan and physical activity schedule.
interventions.rationale: Prevents abrupt glucose fluctuations related to food or exercise.

interventions.action: Assess for beta‑blocker use and coordinate dose adjustments with the physician.
Instruct the patient to report any sweating, tremor, or confusion episodes.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection and timely intervention.

summary.0.quote: Sulfonylureas are a group of diabetes drugs that bind to potassium channels on β cells and stimulate them to produce more insulin.

key_points.0.quote: They are effective in clients with diabetes who have functioning β cells.

key_points.2.quote: Beta blockers can mask the early symptoms of hypoglycemia, such as tachycardia and tremors.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Sulfonylureas are a group of diabetes drugs that bind to potassium channels on β cells and stimulate them to produce more insulin.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Diazoxide Diazoxide is a non-diuretic benzothiadiazine and works by inhibiting insulin release from the pancreas by opening potassium channels in the beta cell membrane.

sections.indications.0.quote: Oral diabetes drugs are used to treat type 2 diabetes.

sections.indications.1.quote: Combination oral diabetes drug therapy is used when monotherapy, diet, and exercise alone cannot control blood glucose levels.

sections.contraindications.1.quote: It is contraindicated for use in clients with severe renal and hepatic impairments (Feingold, 2022).
